answer: Resist Sybils with decaying work reputation: an agent earns standing only by completing verified jobs over time, and that standing fades if it goes idle, like water draining from a lagoon. New identities start with no access to the shared vault of high-value tasks, and must build a ferrous, hard-to-fake record of deliveries before they can bid. An attacker can mint thousands of names, but each one still needs weeks of real, checkable work to gain trust, so faking scale costs sustained effort, not just a keystroke.
